skill.name: ghe-claim
skill.description: Claim a specific GitHub issue after validation. It assigns the issue, updates labels, posts a claim comment, and creates a worktree when needed.
skill.summary: Starts work on a validated GitHub issue and records the claim.
skill.author: Emasoft

security_audit.summary: Most external command detections were false positives caused by Markdown inline-code formatting, not executable backticks. Real concerns remain because the skill permits writes to ~/.claude and contains strong instruction-overriding language that can weaken agent safety. It also requires full reports to be posted to GitHub issue threads, which can disclose sensitive content.

remediation.suggestion: Restrict ~/.claude writes to explicit user confirmation and a precise file allowlist. Remove it from default background-agent permissions.
Remove absolute no-exception language. Clarify that skill instructions never override system, developer, user, or safety policies.
Require confirmation before posting full report content to GitHub. Redact secrets, credentials, and private findings before publication.

content.value_statement: Starting issue work requires validation, labels, comments, and local setup. This skill coordinates those steps for a specific GitHub issue number.
actual_capabilities: Requires a specific issue number before claiming work.
Runs a phase validation step before changing issue state.
Selects a thread manager based on dev, test, or review labels.
Assigns the issue, adds in-progress, and removes ready.
Posts a claim comment with session details.
Creates a development worktree when DEV work requires it.
limitations: It depends on external GitHub and thread manager behavior.
It can modify issue assignment, labels, comments, and local files.
It requires valid repository access and an available issue.
It does not finish or checkpoint work after a claim.

use_cases.title: Begin Development Work
use_cases.description: A developer claims a ready issue and creates the needed worktree before coding.

use_cases.title: Start Test Validation
use_cases.description: A QA engineer claims a test-labeled issue after phase validation confirms prior work is complete.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Review Ownership
use_cases.description: A maintainer claims a review issue and posts a clear session comment for the team.

prompt_templates.title: Claim Development Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate and claim issue #201 for development. Create a worktree if the issue is ready.

prompt_templates.title: Claim With Guardrails
prompt_templates.prompt: Claim issue #201 only if the phase-gate passes. Report any blocker before changing assignment or labels.

prompt_templates.title: Run Full Claim Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: For issue #201, run the claim flow, select the correct thread manager from labels, post the claim comment, and update memory.

output_examples.output: Issue #201 passed phase validation. It was assigned to you, labeled in-progress, and prepared with a development worktree.
Issue #87 was claimed for review. The ready label was removed, a claim comment was posted, and memory was updated.

output_examples.input: Claim #144 but stop if already assigned.
output_examples.output: The claim was not completed because the issue already had an assignee. No labels or comments were changed.

best_practices: Use a clear issue number and confirm the repository context first.
Review the phase-gate result before relying on the claim.
Inspect generated comments before posting sensitive details to GitHub.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to save progress on active work.
Do not claim issues without ready labels or valid phase order.
Do not let it write configuration files without explicit approval.

faq.question: Does this skill require an issue number?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed for a specific GitHub issue number.

faq.question: What changes can it make?
faq.answer: It can assign issues, change labels, post comments, create worktrees, and update memory context.

faq.question: Can it claim an issue that is already assigned?
faq.answer: It should stop during validation when the issue already has an assignee.

faq.question: Does it complete the work?
faq.answer: No. It only starts work by claiming and preparing the issue.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users review first?
faq.answer: Users should review repository access, issue state, and any configuration that allows home directory writes.
